desc:
Given an array nums of positive integers and an integer target, choose two subarrays that do not share any index and whose sums are both exactly target. Return the smallest possible value of the sum of their lengths, or -1 if two such subarrays do not exist.

nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2], target = 3
[3] and [1, 2] (indices 3 and 0..1) have sum 3 each
result = 3
hints: Because all values are positive, for every right end there is at most one left end that gives sum exactly target, and two pointers find all such subarrays in O(n).
Two chosen subarrays do not overlap, so one of them ends before the other starts. When you meet a subarray [l, r], you want the shortest valid subarray that ends before l.
Keep an array best[i] = length of the shortest target-sum subarray that ends at index i or earlier. At each match [l, r] combine best[l - 1] + (r - l + 1).
editorial: With positive numbers the sum of a window grows when it extends right and shrinks when it moves left, so a two-pointer sweep lists every subarray with sum exactly target in O(n). For each right end there is at most one such subarray.

Sweep right to left in index order and maintain best[i], the shortest valid subarray lying entirely inside nums[0..i]; it equals best[i - 1] unless a valid subarray ends at i and is shorter. When a valid subarray [l, r] is found, any partner must lie in nums[0..l-1], so candidate total is best[l - 1] + (r - l + 1). Every pair of disjoint subarrays is considered exactly once with its later subarray as [l, r]. Time O(n), space O(n).
solution:
def minTwoDisjointLength(nums, target):
    n = len(nums)
    INF = 10 ** 9
    best = [INF] * n
    ans = INF
    left = 0
    cur = 0
    for right in range(n):
        cur += nums[right]
        while cur > target:
            cur -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        best[right] = best[right - 1] if right > 0 else INF
        if cur == target:
            length = right - left + 1
            if left > 0 and best[left - 1] < INF:
                ans = min(ans, best[left - 1] + length)
            best[right] = min(best[right], length)
    return -1 if ans >= INF else ans
